newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Nova Scotia Q2 loan losses drop.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Nova Scotia Q2 loan losses drop.

text.p: The Bank of Nova Scotia said on Tuesday that its second quarter provisions for credit losses fell to C$89 million from C$95 million in the second quarter of 1996.

"The full-year specific provision for credit losses is estimated at C$355 million, which is C$25 million lower than last year's provision," Scotia said in a released statement. "The specific provision in the second quarter was C$89 million, a reduction of C$6 million from the same period a year ago."
Scotia said its net impaired loans outstanding decreased by C$326 million from the immediately preceding quarter to C$364 million as at April 30, 1997, or 0.3% of total loans and acceptances.
It said the improvement was partly due to real estate asset sales in the United States and improvements in the Canadian commercial mortgage sector.
